name: RAT - Retrieval Augmented Thoughts (Retrieval Augmented Thoughts Elicit Context-Aware Reasoning in Long-Horizon Generation)
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2403.05313, cs.CL; submitted 8 Mar 2024, v1). No peer-reviewed venue identified; DBLP lists it as a CoRR (arXiv) article. [uncertain] whether it was later published at a conference/journal.
authors_affiliation: Zihao Wang (Peking University), Anji Liu (University of California, Los Angeles / UCLA), Haowei Lin (Peking University), Jiaqi Li (Beijing Institute for General Artificial Intelligence / BIGAI), Xiaojian Ma (Beijing Institute for General Artificial Intelligence / BIGAI), Yitao Liang (Peking University, corresponding author). Affiliated with Team CraftJarvis.
code_url: https://github.com/CraftJarvis/RAT (official implementation by Team CraftJarvis; Python ~50.3% + Jupyter Notebook ~49.7%; ~248 stars, 27 forks as of mid-2025; includes creative.ipynb and a Gradio demo app; requires OPENAI_API_KEY and GOOGLE_API_KEY for Google Search; last commit Apr 2024; no LICENSE file and no releases observed). HuggingFace demo: https://huggingface.co/spaces/jeasinema/RAT.
maintained_repo_url: N/A (single-paper repo, last pushed Apr 2024; not a continuously-updated leaderboard or paper list).
task_domain: Long-horizon generation/reasoning with LLMs across four task families: code generation, mathematical reasoning, creative writing (open-ended text generation), and embodied task planning (Minecraft). Framed as a zero-shot prompting strategy synergizing chain-of-thought (CoT) with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).
problem_setting: Offline, single-model, inference-time (test-time) prompting setting with frozen black-box / open LLMs (GPT-3.5/gpt-3.5-turbo, GPT-4/gpt-4, and CodeLlama-7b). No fine-tuning of the LM or the retriever; off-the-shelf embedding-based retrieval (OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002) over a static corpus, or live Google search for open-web tasks. Single agent, no multi-agent interaction. All experiments are conducted zero-shot (0-demonstration) with the simplest possible prompts and no benchmark examples used as in-context demonstrations. The core problem: long-horizon generation suffers from hallucination and accumulated errors; the method addresses (1) WHAT relevant information to retrieve for complex multi-step reasoning and (2) HOW to correct reasoning steps with retrieved factual information, by iteratively revising each CoT thought step with RAG after an initial zero-shot CoT is generated.
what_is_retrieved: Documents / passages providing factual knowledge to ground and correct each reasoning (thought) step. Sources vary by task: code snippets/notebooks from the codeparrot/github-jupyter dataset (code + math), Minecraft Wiki (minecraft.wiki) and DigMinecraft (www.digminecraft.com) pages (embodied planning), and live Google web search results (creative writing). Not demonstrations, tools, cases, or agent experiences.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus / live web (not a growing agent memory). For code and mathematical reasoning, a fixed external vector library built from the codeparrot/github-jupyter dataset. For embodied planning, fixed external knowledge from the Minecraft Wiki and DigMinecraft websites. For creative writing, the live open web via Google search. There is no episodic/growing memory the agent writes back to; retrieval reads from external knowledge bases or the Internet.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Top-k document retrieval per step (similarity-style ranking via cosine similarity over text-embedding-ada-002 embeddings; for creative writing, top web-search results from Google). The objective is not a formal minimal-complete-set recovery nor a precision-driven variable-size recommendation; however, a stated motivation is that progressive, step-conditioned retrieval ensures more complete coverage of intermediate facts/items (e.g., all intermediary items in a Minecraft plan) than a single task-level query, contrasting classical RAG which over-focuses on the final-target query.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve] only. RAT retrieves documents and uses them to revise a draft thought, but there is no case library, no stored problem-solution cases, and no Retain step. Not a CBR method. (The 'Revise' it performs is revision of the LLM's own draft thoughts with retrieved documents, not revision/adaptation of a retrieved past case.)
explicit_cbr_grounding: False: RAT does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner. It is positioned as a synergy of chain-of-thought prompting and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).
retrieval_unit: Document / passage (a retrieved document or web-page snippet R_i). The iteration/decision unit of generation is the thought step T_i (a CoT step: e.g., a block of pseudo-code with comments, an article outline section, or a sub-goal in an embodied plan), but the retrieved unit itself is a document/passage.
index_source: Static corpus, offline-induced for code and math (a vector index over the codeparrot/github-jupyter dataset using text-embedding-ada-002 embeddings) and for embodied planning (Minecraft Wiki + DigMinecraft pages); live web index for creative writing (Google search engine). No online/test-time growth of the store driven by the agent. A contamination-avoidance pre-processing step (following Guo et al. 2024) is applied to the code library to remove exact benchmark solutions.
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index (semantic embeddings + cosine-similarity nearest-neighbor retrieval over the codeparrot/github-jupyter library) for code/math; a black-box web-search backend (Google) for creative writing; document collections from the Minecraft Wiki / DigMinecraft websites for embodied planning. No graph, hierarchy, or cluster topology is used for organizing the store.
retriever_type: Dense embedding-based retriever (cosine similarity over OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002 embeddings; the preliminary also mentions Sentence-BERT as a possible embedder) for corpus-backed tasks; the Google search engine (black-box web-search API) for open-web creative writing. The ToQuery(.) operator can be a text encoder or an LLM that translates the prompt + current/past thoughts into a query. Off-the-shelf; not trained.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf): neither the embedding model (text-embedding-ada-002) nor the Google search engine is trained or fine-tuned. RAT's novelty is in query construction (using evolving reasoning thoughts as queries) and in WHEN/WHAT to revise, not in learning a retriever. There is no contrastive, LM-feedback, preference, or RL signal applied to the retriever.
query_construction: Reasoning/draft-conditioned query. After an initial zero-shot CoT T = {T_i} is generated, for each step i the query Q_i = ToQuery(I, T_1, ..., T_i) is formed from the task prompt I plus the current and past thought steps; ToQuery(.) is either a text encoder or an LLM that produces a retrieval query. The query thus evolves as reasoning proceeds (autoregressive query refinement), and previously revised thoughts T*_1..T*_{i-1} condition the revision. The motivation: hallucinations often occur only in details (e.g., a wrong date), which still let the search engine find the relevant topic; the draft answer is a better retrieval cue than the bare task prompt.
query_granularity: Step-level (per CoT thought step). A distinct query is constructed for each thought step T_i conditioned on the task prompt and all prior thoughts, rather than one task-level query at t=0. This is contrasted in ablations with the 'non-causal' variant (a single query from the initial reasoning to retrieve everything at once) and with CoT+RAG (whole-CoT-as-query).
when_to_retrieve: Iterative (fixed schedule): after generating the initial zero-shot CoT, RAT retrieves once per thought step and revises each step one by one in causal order (T*_1, then T*_2 conditioned on T*_1, ...). Retrieval is not uncertainty-triggered or learned-router-gated; it occurs at every thought step on a fixed per-step schedule.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule (per-thought-step). Retrieval is triggered deterministically for each step of the initial CoT during the revision pass; there is no token-level confidence, attention/uncertainty, learned complexity classifier, reflection-token, or explicit agent-initiated request signal deciding when to retrieve.
reranking: No dedicated reranking stage. Documents are retrieved by cosine-similarity ranking (or returned by Google search) and the top-ranked k are used directly; no cross-encoder, hierarchy-aware, RRF, or instruction-tuned reranker is described.
retrieved_context_refinement: Query-side / generation-side refinement rather than document distillation. The key processing is (a) using evolving, step-conditioned reasoning thoughts as the retrieval query (iterative query refinement) and (b) using retrieved content to revise/correct the current draft thought step rather than merely summarizing retrieved content (contrasted with classical RAG which 'tends to summarize content retrieved from searches'). No explicit decompose-then-recompose, reason-in-documents distillation, distractor filtering, or compression of retrieved passages is described.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tools/skills; retrieved items are raw documents/passages/web results, not engineered tool descriptions).
index_content_separation: N/A / No: retrieved documents are used directly in the prompt; there is no lightweight-index-then-content progressive-disclosure separation.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool index/protocol). Retrieval uses a static embedding index over codeparrot/github-jupyter, fixed Minecraft Wiki/DigMinecraft pages, and the live Google search API; no MCP/RapidAPI/RESTful/function-calling tool integration with CRUD auto-sync.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no tools are retrieved; RAT retrieves documents/passages, so no inter-tool dependency modeling, dependency graph, or bipartite KG is applicable).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation for iterative revision. Retrieved documents R_i are prepended to the prompt and the LLM revises the current draft thought step: T* <- p_theta(. | I, T*, R_i), where T* accumulates the already-revised prior steps. The revised CoT is then used to produce the final response progressively (step-by-step). No fine-tuning; pure in-context conditioning. Retrieval is used to correct/ground reasoning steps, not to inject demonstrations or skills.
planning_integration: Generate-then-retrieve-then-revise, per-step interleaved. The pipeline is: (1) zero-shot CoT generates an initial draft chain of thoughts T_1..T_n; (2) RAT iterates over steps in causal order, retrieving with a query built from the prompt + current/past thoughts and revising each step T_i -> T*_i conditioned on the already-revised prefix; (3) the response is produced progressively following the revised CoT. No explicit MCTS/tree search; CoT is the reasoning structure (the paper notes ToT-style structures as future work). For embodied planning, the 'plan' is the CoT (a list of sub-goals) that is iteratively revised.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-CoT-step: retrieval and revision are interleaved at the granularity of each chain-of-thought step (e.g., one pseudo-code block, one outline section, one sub-goal). Not per-token, per-sentence, per-tool-call, or per-answer.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not a CBR method; no case adaptation). The analogous operation is execution-/knowledge-free LLM-prompted revision: the LLM rewrites its own draft thought step conditioned on freshly retrieved documents and the revised prefix.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw retrieved document/passage text (code snippets/notebooks, Minecraft Wiki/DigMinecraft page content, or Google search result content) prepended to the prompt as factual context. No distilled strategy, free-text workflow, executable skill, structured note, or latent representation; the injected items are raw documents and the output is the revised free-text/code thought step.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw document/passage (un-distilled factual text/code retrieved from the corpus or web). Not a distilled strategy/insight, state-aware guideline/rule, reusable workflow, procedural skill, demonstration, or hint.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Causal step-by-step revision is the main robustness mechanism: revising each step one-by-one (rather than revising the whole CoT at once) avoids introducing errors at otherwise-correct steps; an ablation (causal vs non-causal) confirms the causal/iterative approach is more reliable. Step-conditioned query refinement also reduces irrelevant retrieval by targeting intermediate, easier-to-retrieve facts. No retriever-aware training, learned relevance evaluator/self-reflection, reason-in-documents refinement, or distractor-aware SFT. The paper explicitly notes (Limitations) that performance still relies on the quality of the external knowledge base and that an inferior/irrelevant KB can yield unhelpful retrieved content.
memory_type: none (no episodic / skill-library / workflow / procedural / graph / latent agent memory). The external corpus/web is a static knowledge source, not a written-to agent memory).
write_back: False: RAT does not store new experiences, cases, or skills into any memory; it only reads from a static external corpus or the live web during inference.
online_growth: No: the retrievable store (codeparrot/github-jupyter index, Minecraft Wiki/DigMinecraft pages, Google web) does not grow as a function of the system's own generation; it is a fixed/external knowledge source.
write_back_trigger: never (no write-back; no memory is maintained or updated).
failure_experience_usage: N/A / none: no storage or retrieval of past failed experiences. The method does correct hallucinations in the current draft (a within-episode self-correction using retrieved facts), but nothing is persisted as failure memory.
memory_evolution_update: N/A (no stored memory entries to mutate; effectively append-only-none).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No: retrieval and per-step triggering follow a fixed schedule with off-the-shelf similarity top-k (or Google search); not an RL-/value-trained policy and not an M-MDP/soft-Q-learning case-selection policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No: single-model, single private retrieval pipeline; no memory/experience shared across agents or heterogeneous frameworks.
benchmarks: Code generation: HumanEval, HumanEval+, MBPP, MBPP+. Mathematical reasoning: GSM8K and GSM-HARD (GSMHard). Creative writing: open-ended tasks including survey/summarization (e.g., the 'summarize the American Civil War according to a timeline' case), evaluated by human Elo/TrueSkill win-rate. Embodied planning: 100 Minecraft tasks (ranging from simple objectives to challenging diamond objectives) evaluated through MC-TextWorld (Lin et al. 2023).
benchmark_family: code (HumanEval/HumanEval+/MBPP/MBPP+) + math/QA-style (GSM8K, GSM-HARD) + open-ended creative writing (custom, human-rated) + embodied (Minecraft via MC-TextWorld). Spans the code and embodied (Minecraft) families plus math reasoning and open-ended generation; not the standard web/tool/memory-agent benchmark families.
baselines: DIRECT (the base LLM answering directly, no retrieval/CoT); zero-shot CoT (Kojima et al. 2022, 'let's think step by step'); RAG with n retrieved examples in single-shot (RAG-1 shot) and multi-shot (RAG-5 shot) configurations (Lewis et al. 2020). All baselines use the same base model per setting and no benchmark examples as demonstrations. Ablation baselines additionally include RAG-1 (question-as-query) and CoT+RAG (whole-CoT-as-query).
key_metrics: Code generation: pass@k (pass@1, pass@5). Mathematical reasoning: accuracy (per-question, aligned with GSM8K). Embodied planning: plan execution success rate in MC-TextWorld (executability) and human Elo/TrueSkill rating (plausibility). Creative writing: human Elo evaluation -> TrueSkill rating score (Herbrich et al. 2006) and win rate. Reported relative improvements vs DIRECT are also a headline summary metric.
headline_result: Relative average improvements of RAT over DIRECT across base models/tasks: +13.63% on code generation, +16.96% on mathematical reasoning, +19.2% on creative writing, and +42.78% on embodied (Minecraft) task planning. Concrete examples: on HumanEval (GPT-4 base) RAT reaches pass@1 69.33% / pass@5 88.40% (vs DIRECT 57.32% / 78.66%, i.e. +20.94% / +12.38% relative on pass@1/pass@5); on GSM8K RAT 71.36% vs DIRECT 65.85% (GPT-3.5); on Minecraft embodied planning (GPT-4) RAT achieves 76.67±8.02% executability and a 29.37 TrueSkill plausibility rating (+42.78% relative), the best among all methods.
ablations: (1) Retrieval-strategy ablation (Table 3, HumanEval/HumanEval+): RAG-1 (question-as-query) < CoT+RAG (whole-CoT-as-query) < RAT (continuously-modified reasoning-thought parts as queries); RAT yields +8.7 percentage points pass@1 and +7.9 pp pass@5 over the RAG-1 baseline on HumanEval, showing iterative query refinement drives the gain. (2) Causal vs non-causal reasoning ablation (Table 4, CoT baseline): the causal method (iteratively interleaving reasoning and retrieval, revising step-by-step) beats CoT by +11.9 pp pass@1 and +4.6 pp pass@5 on HumanEval and outperforms the non-causal variant (use initial reasoning to retrieve all steps at once then generate final answer), establishing the value of sequential, causal reason-and-retrieve. (3) Cross-model generalization (Table 1): RAT improves CodeLlama-7b, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4; the largest gains are with GPT-4 (better in-context learning from retrieved text), while CodeLlama-7b shows degradation on MBPP+ (pass@1 -5.05% relative), attributed to weaker in-context learning of smaller models. (4) Case analyses on Minecraft (crafting-table materials) and the American Civil War timeline illustrate how step-wise retrieval recovers intermediary facts and corrects detail-level hallucinations that classical RAG misses.
evaluation_decoupling: No: only end-to-end task metrics (pass@k, accuracy, executability, TrueSkill/win-rate) are reported. No separate intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / completeness) are measured for the retriever.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Mostly outcome metrics (final code pass@k, math accuracy, generation quality ratings). Some process-oriented signal is captured via embodied-planning executability (plan execution success rate, a step-wise feasibility proxy) and via qualitative case analyses of intermediate-step correctness/hallucination, but there is no formal scored reasoning-faithfulness or step-wise retrieval-accuracy metric.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Limited quantitative cost reporting. RAT performs one retrieval + one LLM revision call per CoT thought step plus the initial zero-shot CoT, so cost scales with the number of thought steps (more LLM/embedding/search calls than single-shot RAG). The paper notes in Limitations that maintaining and retrieving from a very large knowledge base is expensive and can hurt retrieval precision, and that step-by-step thinking can be redundant for straightforward questions. No explicit latency/dollar/token-count numbers, retrieval-call counts, or speedup figures are reported. [uncertain] exact per-task call counts and latency.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed top-k retrieval per step (top-ranked k documents by cosine similarity fed into the prompt; Google returns top web results for creative writing). The paper does not specify exact k values or a token budget cap per injected context in the main text; k appears fixed rather than adaptive/precision-driven. [uncertain] the exact k and token budget per task.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A as a new-benchmark contribution; RAT uses existing benchmarks (HumanEval/HumanEval+/MBPP/MBPP+, GSM8K/GSM-HARD, MC-TextWorld Minecraft 100-task suite) plus a custom set of open-ended creative-writing tasks evaluated by human Elo/TrueSkill. The Minecraft evaluation uses 100 tasks ranging from simple to diamond-level objectives. A benchmark-contamination pre-processing step (following Guo et al. 2024) removes exact solutions from the code library; discussed in Appendix D.
builds_on: Chain-of-Thought / zero-shot CoT prompting (Wei et al. 2022; Kojima et al. 2022 'let's think step by step'); Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Lewis et al. 2020 RAG); iterative/interleaved retrieval-with-reasoning predecessors -- IRCoT (Trivedi et al. 2022, CoT to generate better queries), IRGR / entailment-tree iterative retrieval-generation reasoner (Ribeiro et al. 2022), and ITRG (Feng et al. 2023, retrieval based on last-step generation); embedding/text-encoder retrieval (Sentence-BERT, Reimers & Gurevych 2019; OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002). Base models: CodeLlama-7b (Roziere et al. 2023), gpt-3.5-turbo (Ouyang et al. 2022), GPT-4 (OpenAI 2023). Evaluation infra: MC-TextWorld (Lin et al. 2023), TrueSkill (Herbrich et al. 2006).
contrasts_with: Classical single-query RAG (RAG-1/RAG-5) which uses one query (the task prompt / question) and tends to summarize retrieved content, over-focusing on the final-target item and missing intermediary facts; zero-shot CoT alone which hallucinates intermediate steps (e.g., wrong crafting materials, wrong dates); prior reasoning-augmented RAG (IRCoT, IRGR, ITRG) which 'simply adopt a single query' or retrieve for single-step QA. RAT's distinctions: (1) generate a full zero-shot CoT first, then (2) retrieve using evolving reasoning + draft answers as queries in an autoregressive way, and (3) causally revise each thought step one-by-one rather than revising the whole CoT at once or retrieving everything up front.
lineage: Group B (RAG for task solving) -- iterative/test-time retrieval interleaved with chain-of-thought reasoning. RAT sits in the lineage of reasoning-interleaved RAG (IRCoT, ITRG, IRGR) and is contemporaneous with active/adaptive RAG (FLARE, Self-RAG, Adaptive-RAG), but is distinguished by being a zero-shot prompting strategy that generates a draft CoT and then iteratively, causally revises each thought step with step-conditioned retrieval, extending RAG from short-form QA to diverse long-horizon generation (code, math, writing, embodied Minecraft planning).
